insights.claim: The acquisition system generated high volume, but most of the volume is low or medium-low quality: A/B leads are 29.9% and Tier A is 4.4%.
June scaled volume materially without improving the A/B mix: June produced 776 leads and 229 A/B leads, with a 29.5% A/B rate.
The strongest quality separator is declared travel commitment and timing: leads with tickets already bought produce 88.7% A/B and 26.6% Tier A; solo-looking leads produce 5.7% A/B and 0% Tier A.
Retargeting/activation has better quality rate than cold capture but lower scale and higher observed matched cost per A/B lead.
Two commercial ads dominate both volume and quality contribution, creating dependency: ViajeSinEstres and ViajaComoInvitado generate 1002 leads and 288 A/B leads.
Several smaller assets have stronger quality rates, especially FiltroBilletes variants, but sample sizes are smaller and should not be treated as definitive winners.

The main trade-off is scale versus quality density: cold commercial capture supplies most leads and lowest commercial matched cost, while activation and intent-filtering assets supply denser A/B and Tier A signals at lower scale.

analytical_narrative: AUC-001 shows a system that has learned to buy volume efficiently, but has not yet concentrated enough of that volume in high-intent demand. The best quality signals are not generic creative performance signals; they are declared commercial maturity signals: tickets, near-term travel timing and a more complete/private experience need. The operational challenge is not simply lowering cost per lead, but increasing the share of spend and learning signal attached to those high-intent combinations without losing the scale currently provided by commercial capture.
risks: Optimizing on generic CPL would reward volume that is mostly C/D.
Treating attention campaigns as direct lead generators would violate FARO campaign-signal interpretation.
Creative winners cannot be declared causally with the current evidence.
Absence of CRM/revenue prevents validation of post-lead commercial conversion.
unknowns: Commercial conversion, revenue and opportunity quality after lead capture.
Whether weekly changes represent learning, fatigue, budget effects or normal volatility.
